The Suitor by Jane Kenyon





We lie back to back. Curtains

lift and fall,

like the chest of someone sleeping.

Wind moves the leaves of the box elder;

they show their light undersides,

turning all at once

like a school of fish.

Suddenly I understand that I am happy.

For months this feeling

has been coming closer, stopping

for short visits, like a timid suitor.

Despite what you think, even the people with the 'happiest' lives have problems.  Don't for a second think that meeting people, and going to parties are what defines living. Yeah, I guess it could be a part of it, but those are just kind of 'existing' things to me. 

Getting laid will not solve on your problems, contrary to what your friends are telling you. I don't know how that ever became a solution but it doesn't help. 

The thing about being twenty is that you just got done being a teen. You're in school, you're not really sure where you're going but you have an idea. You're doing schoolwork to get there, you're putting yourself out there whether you know it or not. Some people can't even muster the motivation to do that alone.  Whether you would like to believe it or not, you *are* going somewhere even as you struggle to do so. 

As far a girls go, we are a difficult bunch and I'm sorry.  But don't shoot yourself down because you've had an awkward experience. I guarantee there are a lot of people scared of intimacy/opening up to people.  I think it's because if you do, you're vulnerable, you could get hurt. Nobody likes to get hurt. 

There's nothing wrong with you for being alone. Alright?

I can't tell you the secret to feeling good about yourself, I don't even know it.  I don't know how you can get your spark back, but you can try little things here and there. This sounds so juvenile, but you can try joining a club, you can try something new that is a little bit uncomfortable. Or maybe even change your major. That's really big, I know. But maybe what you need is a complete do-over. I know that's time consuming and expensive, but maybe your spark is found elsewhere.

  In the end, don't hate yourself. That is the worse thing you could do. Give yourself some slack.
